react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism as the dominant biological signature in the treatment group. RaMP-DB multi-DB ORA assigned this pathway the top rank with FDR = 1.3 × 10⁻⁸ and a fold-enrichment of 758, driven by four input metabolites — L-glutamic acid (C00025), dihydrolipoate (C02147), choline (C00114), and L-threonine (C00188). The m/z-network method (mummichog) independently ranked the same pathway first (p = 0.00168), with a perfect overlap of 6 matched network nodes including the four input compounds. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed the KEGG-namespace hit (hsa00260, p = 0.004), again implicating choline and L-threonine. Across these three independent paradigms, the amino-acid metabolism axis is the only pathway hitting within the top 3 of every tool. Secondary convergent signals included Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (RaMP rank 8, KEGG hsa00760 in MetaboAnalystR, mummichog rank 1) and Nitrogen metabolism (RaMP rank 6, MetaboAnalystR rank 1), both supported by niacinamide and L-glutamic acid, suggesting a broader perturbation of nitrogen-handling biochemistry. The driver metabolites L-threonine (direct entry point into serine/glycine biosynthesis via threonine aldolase) and L-glutamic acid (central transamination hub) anchor the most confident finding.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of the 9-metabolite differential set (pyruvate, oxoglutarate, L-glutamate, phosphate, isopentenyl pyrophosphate, niacinamide, dihydrolipoate, choline, L-threonine) identified two robustly enriched pathways supported by at least two independent methods. The top consensus hit is Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260), which achieves rank 0 in both the RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 1.30 × 10⁻⁸) and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 0.004), and rank 0 in Mummichog (p = 0.004) using the empirical-compound network. The driver metabolites are choline (KEGG:C00114), L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025), and dihydrolipoate (KEGG:C02147), all resolved in the metabolites_hit rosters of the enrichment results. The second consensus hit is Nitrogen metabolism (KEGG:map00910), which appears at rank 6 in RaMP ORA (FDR = 6.0 × 10⁻⁴) and rank 1 in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p = 0.019); its driver is L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025) with dihydrolipoate (KEGG:C02147) as a secondary hit. A third convergent signal is Vitamin B3 (nicotinate and nicotinamide) metabolism (KEGG:map00910 / hsa00760), present in RaMP ORA (rank 8, FDR = 7.0 × 10⁻⁴), MetaboAnalystR (rank 5, p = 0.046), and Mummichog (rank 1, p = 0.015); niacinamide (KEGG:C00153) is the primary driver with L-glutamic acid as a shared hit. The amino-acid hub centred on L-glutamic acid is the common node across all three consensus pathways, connecting nitrogen disposal, threonine catabolism, and nicotinamide salvage. Five of the nine input metabolites (L-glutamic acid, L-threonine, choline, niacinamide, dihydrolipoate) map directly to at least one consensus pathway hit; phosphate, pyruvate, oxoglutarate, and isopentenyl pyrophosphate did not reach significance in the ORA or PSEA analyses, and their inclusion did not alter the top-ranked pathway scores. Limitations: the query_pathway_members tool could not validate KEGG/Reactome namespace compound rosters (only HUMAN1/RECON2 are indexed), so driver-metabolite membership is inferred from the embedded metabolites_hit lists in the EnrichmentResults. FELLA RWR and sspa ORA were unavailable at runtime, limiting the network-diffusion perspective.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism as the dominant biological signature in the treatment group. RaMP-DB multi-DB ORA assigned this pathway the top rank with FDR = 1.3 × 10⁻⁸ and a fold-enrichment of 758, driven by four input metabolites — L-glutamic acid (C00025), dihydrolipoate (C02147), choline (C00114), and L-threonine (C00188). The m/z-network method (mummichog) independently ranked the same pathway first (p = 0.00168), with a perfect overlap of 6 matched network nodes including the four input compounds. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed the KEGG-namespace hit (hsa00260, p = 0.004), again implicating choline and L-threonine. Across these three independent paradigms, the amino-acid metabolism axis is the only pathway hitting within the top 3 of every tool. Secondary convergent signals included Nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (RaMP rank 8, KEGG hsa00760 in MetaboAnalystR, mummichog rank 1) and Nitrogen metabolism (RaMP rank 6, MetaboAnalystR rank 1), both supported by niacinamide and L-glutamic acid, suggesting a broader perturbation of nitrogen-handling biochemistry. The driver metabolites L-threonine (direct entry point into serine/glycine biosynthesis via threonine aldolase) and L-glutamic acid (central transamination hub) anchor the most confident finding.
